raw.assessment: The incumbent provides staffed key access and telephone/in-person booking; eleven groups obtained weekly bookings (H4-O1). Its strongest plausible account is predictable recurring access with modest coordination resources. Success is unproven: needs and acceptable alternatives were not recorded, three access conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly (H4-O3/O4/O6/O7). The concrete limiting observation is H4-O5: the only piano is in one room, while most equipment entries are blank. Thus 68% aggregate reservation utilization (H4-O2) cannot establish that refused requests could use spare capacity. Evening concentration and missed starts suggest distinct possible constraints, not established causes.

openings.claim: Would recording complete acceptable windows, rehearsal duration needs and necessary equipment reveal a feasible allocation that inherited 90-minute bookings conceal?
openings.delta: Distinguish scheduling rigidity from genuine scarcity of compatible room-time, while counting unmet needs rather than successful reservations alone.
openings.prediction: If inherited times or durations constrain access, a flexible allocation will meet more stated needs with identical resources. If compatible demand exceeds supply, unsatisfied requests will remain concentrated in overlapping equipment/time requirements.
openings.probe: Use each contact's short conversation to record needs, acceptable windows and equipment. Construct a shadow eight-week schedule using two rooms, existing staffed hours and equipment, preserving both performances and each requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Compare feasible coverage under inherited bookings versus movable bookings; do not implement an infeasible allocation or count outside rehearsals as building provision.
assumptions: Contacts can describe group requirements accurately.
Changing inherited reservations requires agreement; shadow feasibility does not establish uptake.

openings.claim: An authoritative booking record with unique reservation identifiers and explicit confirmation of each change may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Make each telephone or desk change traceable through confirmation and calendar copying.
openings.prediction: If ambiguous change handling causes conflicts, discrepancies and duplicate expectations should decline; persistent conflicts with matching records would weaken that explanation.
openings.probe: Pilot one authoritative paper record: log each change once, confirm room/time verbally with its identifier, update the online copy, and check desk key release against the master. Track disagreements, arrival expectations and total administration minutes across eight weeks, including pilot work.
assumptions: Staff can consult the master before confirming access.
Extra logging may exceed the two-hour administration target and must be measured.

raw.assessment: The observations establish uneven access, late or missed sessions, booking conflicts, and variable administration time. They do not establish whether spare room-hours coincide with usable rehearsal opportunities. The following capability is speculative; eight-week success and administrative feasibility remain unproven.

openings.claim: A hypothetical ensemble-aware booking broker could detect when two differently named groups depend on the same indispensable musician and propose confirmed exchanges that make both rehearsals attendable. Its presently testable partial capability is identifying group pairs that cannot actually rehearse simultaneously.
openings.delta: Extend the booking unit from a group name to its minimum viable attendance conditions. A room vacancy alone would no longer count as a usable alternative. Full operation would require accurate attendance constraints, acceptable windows, equipment requirements, exchange consent, and one authoritative booking record.
openings.prediction: If indispensable shared membership contributes to unusable bookings, contacts will identify specific overlapping reservations that could not both proceed with the required players; these should correspond to documented late or missed sessions more often than comparable reservations without such overlap. No identified overlap would weaken this explanation.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or in-person conversations with the twelve contacts to request group-pair incompatibilities and retrospective reasons for the fourteen late or missed sessions; personal musician names are unnecessary. Compare those reports with the existing calendars. On paper, attempt one mutually acceptable exchange for an identified pair, checking equipment and windows. Record conversation and scheduling minutes. This tests detection and exchange feasibility; it does not establish the eight-week outcome.
assumptions: Shared indispensable players exist and contacts can report incompatibilities accurately; neither is established.
Any enacted exchange preserves every requesting group’s weekly 60-minute access, the two performances, existing equipment, fees, rooms, and staffed hours.
Changes require confirmation through telephone or in-person channels and a synchronized authoritative record.
The full capability would need to reduce other administration enough to average at most two hours weekly; that dependency must be measured rather than assumed.

openings.claim: Inherited times or 90-minute durations may conceal feasible allocation.
openings.discriminator: Improved coverage with movable bookings supports rigidity; persistent equipment/window overlap supports scarcity.
openings.probe: Interview contacts for total needs, durations, windows and equipment; compare inherited and movable shadow eight-week schedules. Exclude outside rehearsals from building provision.
openings.uncertainty: Requirements may be inaccurate; feasibility does not establish agreement or uptake.

openings.claim: One authoritative record, reservation IDs and confirmed changes may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.discriminator: Fewer discrepancies supports change-handling explanation; conflicts despite matching records weaken it.
openings.probe: Pilot paper master, verbal room/time/ID confirmation, synchronized online copy and key-release checks; track discrepancies, arrival expectations and all administration for eight weeks.
openings.uncertainty: Staff consultation and workload feasibility are unproven; logging may exceed two hours weekly.

openings.claim: Indispensable shared musicians may make simultaneous bookings unusable; identifying incompatible group pairs could enable agreed exchanges.
openings.discriminator: Pair incompatibilities corresponding to late/missed sessions more often than comparable nonoverlaps support explanation; absent overlap weakens it.
openings.probe: Ask twelve contacts for pair incompatibilities and causes of fourteen late/missed sessions without musician names; compare calendars. Attempt one mutually acceptable exchange on paper, checking windows/equipment; record minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Shared players and report accuracy are unestablished. Detection/exchange feasibility does not validate a full broker or eight-week success; administration savings remain necessary.

post_distill.decision: Probe all three; success remains unproven. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, equipment, no new fees, both performances, requested weekly 60-minute entitlement and telephone/in-person access. Enacted changes require agreement and authoritative confirmation. Reject infeasible allocations. Evaluate eight-week coverage >=90%, conflicts <2 and administration <=2 hours/week, including probe work.
